output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the past 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354%, and the upper edge of the normal band is 0.482%, so 0.411% sits inside it. Three earlier weeks were higher, and investigations of those found no fault. The burn-rate alert did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard count matches the raw logs, so this isn't a counting artefact. The "new pods error twice as much" finding is a warm-up effect. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image, shows new pods at about 0.5% against old pods at about 0.3%, because their caches start empty. That adds only 10–20 errors, so it says nothing about v4.18 being faulty. Bookings and support complaints did not change. My advice is not to roll back, and not to mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as normal and apply the standard check to next week. I'm fairly confident, but I did not rule out the replica move or partner-sync traffic as small contributors. If next week exceeds the band, investigate then.
